articles.title: Reviewing NHL Trade Rumors Before 2026 Opening Week
articles.summary: With the 2026 NHL season set to begin next week, the rumor mill is heating up.
articles.body:
With the 2026 NHL season set to begin next week, the rumor mill is heating up.

In Detroit, Dylan Larkin's situation is drawing attention. It has been several months since Larkin requested a trade. Meanwhile, Winnipeg Jets star netminder Connor Hellebuyck has also publicly requested a trade.

Below, we'll take a closer look at these rumors and what might unfold.

Kirill Marchenko's status in Columbus is a major storyline as he enters the final year of his contract in the 2026-27 season.

According to The Athletic's Aaron Portzline , Marchenko's agent has already stated that he does not plan to re-sign with the Blue Jackets.

On his 32 Thoughts podcast, Elliotte Friedman reported that the Toronto Maple Leafs are interested in Marchenko, along with the Islanders, Bruins, Canadiens, Jets, Golden Knights, and Kraken.

Marchenko led the team in goals last season and recorded 67 points. Marchenko's public disinterest in re-signing with Columbus makes a trade likely, especially considering there is only one year left on his contract.

It has now been several months since Dylan Larkin's trade request was first reported.

The Red Wings are still searching for a new general manager after Steve Yzerman abruptly stepped down in July, leaving more questions than answers.

Vegas, Minnesota, and Florida all emerged as the three teams Larkin had his eyes on. But that list has now expanded. In the latest episode of his 32 Thoughts Podcast , Elliotte Friedman reported that Larkin's list of trade destinations now includes Colorado, Washington, Dallas, and Tampa Bay.

Larkin has five seasons left on a contract that'll see him make $8.70 million annually. He's coming off his fifth straight season with 30+ goals and 30+ assists, and it's likely he's shipped off in the coming months to a team like Colorado or Vegas, who could view him as the missing piece and bolster their offer.

On August 27, Connor Hellebuyck publicly requested a trade , bringing months of speculation about his future with the Winnipeg Jets to an end.

Hellebuyck is widely recognized as one of the best American-born netminders in NHL history with three Vezina Trophies and an Olympic Gold Medal.

As such, trading a player like him is far from simple. Furthermore, several factors have slowed the process.

The main obstacle is his contract, which pays him $8.5 million per year for the next five seasons. At 32 years old, can he continue to be among the best goalies in the league? Last season, Hellebbuyck posted a save percentage under .900 for the first time in his career. He recorded just 5.5 goals saved above expected, a steep drop from his NHL-best 39.6 in 2024-25.

Performance aside, Jets general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff has expressed that he is taking his time and considering every option. As such, it appears that Hellebuyck will remain with the Jets until a suitable trade offer emerges.

articles.title: BS Meter on CM Punk, Seth Rollins Rumored MITB Plans, AEW Expiring Contracts and New Adds, More
articles.summary: A hot stretch for the pro wrestling rumor mill just keeps ramping up in temperature.
articles.body:
A hot stretch for the pro wrestling rumor mill just keeps ramping up in temperature.

Some of it is the upped competition on the calendar itself, with World's Collide and All Out essentially going head-to-head at a time of year typically reserved for a "break" of sorts.

Much of it, though, is just simple eyebrow-raising rumors. Think free agents possibly joining new promotions, Penta's rising star and possible big returns for the upcoming Money in the Bank PLE, to name a few.

To help fans keep pace with all the buzz of the rumor mill, let's place the must-know rumors on the BS Meter, with 10 being the highest form of unbelievable buzz fans can safely dismiss.

There are more names than usual perhaps headed to free agency. According to Fightful Select (h/t Cain A. Knight of Cageside Seats), Anthony Bowens and Max Caster are both on the way to free agency with no talks about new deals in the rumblings.

It feels like the internet has had a grip on Bowens possibly being a WWE target for a long time now. Either, really, would make sense as guys who might want to jump ship and see if their star could rise further in WWE.

Buy this one on all counts. AEW has a sort of bloated-feeling roster right now, so they might not be in a hurry to do early re-signings. And looking at WWE, it's hard to ignore the fast rise for Royce Keyes, so other wrestlers might want to take similar chances.

The other side of this coin is AEW going after free agents. According to Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp (h/t Knight ), Ilja Dragunov will sign when visa formalities get wrapped up, while Kairi Sane's status remains up in the air.

Both Dragunov and Sane, on the other hand, always felt like they would take this pipeline the other direction, landing in AEW's orbit. Dragunov feels like a natural for the main roster there, while Sane could always land AEW-adjacent overseas and still work with the company.

Dragunov seems like a formality and he'll be a great fit, obviously. But Sane has always felt like the much bigger deal. It wouldn't be a shock to see her debut in Japan first, not necessarily as an AEW-centric wrestler.

Penta is on the rise. According to WrestleVotes Radio (h/t Knight ), Penta's showing against Roman Reigns in Mexico City was so good that big plans have changed around the main-event scene.

No kidding. Talk about a star-making showing on that episode of Raw. It's a little jaded to think that this is conveniently coming about right near the men's Money in the Bank ladder match before Penta takes the briefcase. But sometimes, the eyes don't lie: Penta was just that good as an obvious main-event presence.

Very easy to buy into the idea that Penta's match against Reigns was planned as a one-off thing initially. That needs to change now, as it's pretty clear WWE has, not just a merch-mover, but a main-event star on its hands. Nobody is saying Penta should actually beat Reigns, but it's clear WWE needs to try to bottle the lightning here.

How close is Seth Rollins? According to WrestleVotes (h/t Knight ), the one-off showing at a live event in South America wasn't meant to suggest he's back full-go because the right creative hasn't emerged yet.

The rumor goes on to state that Rollins initially had a role in the Money in the Bank match, but that's now up in the air. And while it might sound weird, Rollins' brief return recently never felt like a full return, if that makes sense.

Fair enough. Rollins' "real" return will probably feature big storyline implications right away. And with so many names like Kevin Owens and now Penta floating around main-event scenes, it makes sense if WWE is still finding the right creative fit at this point in time.

Is CM Punk about to miss a major event? According to WrestleVotes (h/t Knight ), there was an outside chance that Punk wouldn't work the Money in the Bank show at all.

Punk won the triple threat qualifying match for the men's Money in the Bank match. Before that episode of SmackDown, there wasn't an actual title match planned for the PLE yet. This is pro wrestling, so maybe there's still a swerve coming here, though?

articles.title: Making the Case For LA Knight to Join Royce Keys' 946 Faction on WWE Raw
articles.summary: In WWE, LA Knight is an odd case: Right now, he's in a top title program with Roman Reigns, yet it still feels like he's floating in a bit of purgatory.
articles.body:
In WWE, LA Knight is an odd case: Right now, he's in a top title program with Roman Reigns, yet it still feels like he's floating in a bit of purgatory.

Compelling, really. Knight has never won the big one and it doesn't feel like that is going to change. His recent promo on an episode of WWE's Raw showed him in a more vulnerable state, admitting these types of things and even making a few awkward pauses, perhaps to play with the idea of forgetting his lines.

So, a proposal: Let's get Knight involved with Royce Keyes and the fast-rising 946 faction.

Second, the hook: Knight is going to lose again. He's not going to go out and top Reigns in a match at Money in the Bank. And if he were, for whatever reason, one could easily see him getting cashed-in on by the briefcase winner from the same night, putting his one and only reign as lasting a matter of minutes.

Unless an outside element like Keyes gets involved.

There are elements in Knight's promo, after all, mentioning that Reigns hasn't had much in the way of outside help during his title matches lately. That could change at Money in the Bank. Knight, then, would need some backup.

The narrative draw is simple enough. Knight is bound to at least have a competitive match with Reigns. If Keyes and Co. throw interference that messes up Knight's big chance, there's bound to be some tension there. But at the same time, he could use the help of a faction against the overall Bloodline.

Call it a nice cherry on top for WWE. Onlookers have rightfully criticized WWE for slamming unnecessary, weird faction drama into the calendar this time of year to prep for Survivor Series. Knight needing some help because he's getting ganged up on by the Bloodline sort of just fits right now.

An uneasy alliance with 946 for Knight could boost Keyes' star, too. A little inter-faction tension never hurts and this wouldn't be an exception. Maybe, in the process of making this work, Knight gradually shifts into what feels like an overdue heel turn, too.

At this point, this is just sort of where things sit for Knight. He's not fighting CM Punk or Cody Rhodes, who have dropped titles in recent times unexpectedly to boost other Superstars.

Plus, the overall landscape is starting to pass Knight by. He's had repeated chances to win the big one. Now, Keyes is shooting up the board quickly. Penta just put on a match with Reigns that made him a main-event presence for good. Punk and Rhodes are still there. Solo Sikoa has raised some eyebrows. Oba Femi and Bron Breakker are on the rise. That's just mentioning a few names, and there's only so much time before the long-term plans for WrestleMania need to start forming.

Sure, steering Knight into faction territory and not letting him win it all wil sting for his hardcore fans. But there are worse positions to find oneself in WWE. Ask Dominik Mysterio how he's doing right now after his wild fall down the board after initially looking like a main-event guy.

There are worse positions, especially for someone like Knight, too. Internet fans tend to spotlight his botches, especially with those pesky turnbuckles, and he's felt like a bit of a community project for online fans since the WWE Unreal stuff that showed some of his backstage interactions with the likes of Triple H.

In theory, WWE would like fans to think that Knight can actually beat Reigns. Or even that Keyes and other faction drama, plus a briefcase, can lead to some unpredictable things at Money in the Bank.

But the reality is probably something closer to an uneasy alliance that shoves Knight into Keyes' group temporarily before a feud blossoms out of that over time. This is less Reigns' fault than it is just simple logistics when taking into account the entirety of the main-event scene at this point.

If nothing else, Knight would remain on the outskirts of the main-event scene this way and his appearances wouldn't be repetitive throughout the winter. It's not the ceiling many fans want to see for Knight, but it sure beats the tag and/or random feud purgatory most of the WWE roster gets, with bonus points for keeping the hot new faction relevant in a big way, too.

articles.title: How to Watch the Iowa Hawkeyes at Michigan Wolverines
articles.summary: The Hawkeyes hit the road for the first time in 2026 as then square off with the Michigan Wolverines in Ann Arbor.
articles.body:
The training wheels come off today. Your #17 Iowa Hawkeyes open Big Ten play with their first road trip of the season. As if that wasn't difficult enough, it's the front end of as daunting a three-game stretch as any team in the country will face this year: at #18 Michigan today, #7 Ohio State at Kinnick next Saturday, then a short-week trip to Washington the following Friday. The season's ceiling gets defined over these next three weeks and it all starts today.

Iowa arrives 3-0 and rolling after their dominant non-conference finale performance. The Hawkeyes thumped Northern Iowa 55-0 while resting DJ Vonnahme , Kamari Moulton and L.J. Phillips Jr. Despite the starters sitting on offense, Iowa still ran for 422 yards behind three different 100-yard rushers, the first time that's happened in 40 years. Xavier Williams alone went for 151 and three scores on just six carries.

Perhaps more important than the impressive showing on the ground was what we learned under center as the quarterback question is finally answered. Hank Brown was listed atop the week four depth chart with the "OR" finally gone after a literally perfect day against UNI: 12-for-12 for 153 yards and two touchdowns. On the season he's completing 72.6% of his passes for 473 yards and three scores without a turnover, a start no Iowa quarterback has ever matched through three games. The catch: he has never started a road game at any level, and his first one comes in the largest stadium in the country.

Michigan enters the day technically unbeaten, just like the Hawkeyes. But the Wolverines ' 3-0 has come with much more drama. Kyle Whittingham's first win in Ann Arbor needed a disputed final play to survive Western Michigan.

The Wolverines bounced back from what will forever be an asterisk win to look much better in their win over then-#11 Oklahoma . They wrapped up their non-conference slate by sleeping through a half against UTEP before finally looking like the kind of team we thought they could be in the preseason.

The offense has sputtered despite the millions spent to acquire Bryce Underwood : Michigan sits 62nd nationally in scoring (27.3 per game) and 98th in total offense. Underwood is completing 62.5% of his throws with three touchdowns against one interception and he leads the team in rushing with just 156 yards on the season.

While the numbers aren't impressive for a season rushing total, Underwood's legs are still the thing that can beat you, which makes the assignment for Iowa's defensive ends the same one they aced two weeks ago: keep the quarterback in the pocket without letting him get comfortable. Jaylen Raynor managed 18 yards on 8 carries in that dress rehearsal, but Iowa also never sacked him. Phil Parker will want both halves of the equation this time.

Expect points to be scarce. Both of these defenses rank top-20 nationally in scoring and top-10 in total defense, and the best comp we have is fresh: Iowa State's defense ranks right alongside Michigan's in both categories, and Iowa managed 16 points and 284 yards in the Cy-Hawk game. The books agree, with the line opening at Michigan -4.5 and nudging to -5.5 later in the week, with the over/under sitting at just 38.5 total points.

Then there's the history. Today is the 65th all-time meeting, and Michigan leads the series 45-15-4 with four straight wins, though the teams haven't met in the regular season since 2022. Iowa's last win was Keith Duncan 's 14-13 walk-off against a #2-ranked Michigan team at Kinnick a decade ago, and the Hawkeyes haven't won in the Big House since 2010, which also stands as the last time Iowa won a game in front of 100,000-plus fans anywhere. No pressure, Hank.

As we countdown to kickoff, here's everything you need to know about today's matchup.

articles.title: Miami injury report: Is Malachi Toney playing vs Central Michigan?
articles.summary: The Miami Hurricanes got banged up last week vs Wake Forest. Here's the latest news on Malachi Toney and Mark Flecther's status and whether they play today.
articles.body:
Miami won at Wake Forest, but it cost them dearly. And with injuries limiting Heisman contender Malachi Toney and taking punishing running back Mark Fletcher Jr. out of the game, Hurricanes fans are hoping the extra day off means they're back and ready to play their normal snaps today against Central Michigan .

Toney was never the same after stretching backward to make a catch in the third quarter of the Sept. 18 game against the Demon Deacons. The Canes' leading receiver, second in the nation with 28 catches for 444 yards and tied for fourth with five touchdowns, was used sparingly after that as Darian Mensah and the offense stagnated.

Part of that was the subsequent loss of Fletcher, who left during the fourth quarter with an upper-body injury . The senior is Miami's leading rusher with 230 yards and three TDs on 36 carries. Without them and other key offensive pieces, the Canes had to scrap to hold on for the 33-20 win.

Miami football vs Wake Forest: Photos from ACC Friday night matchup

Two major players on the offense were lost for the season when running back Marty Brown (knee) and wide receiver Joshua Moore (upper body) were among those injured . Brown was the No. 2 running back with 97 yards and a touchdown through three games. Moore was second behind Toney with 107 receiving yards and two TDs, and he placed fourth with seven catches. Tight end Elija Lofton also got banged up and briefly left at the end of the first half.

Here's the latest on Miami's injuries, who's expected to play and which absences could impact the game. Will Malachi Toney and Mark Fletcher play?

Toney is expected to play Saturday vs. Central Michigan . If he is unavailable, Miami will rely on Daylyn Upshaw and Cooper Barkate as the primary receiving options, meaning CMU can focus more on underneath coverage.

Fletcher is expected to play Saturday vs. Central Michigan. If he is unavailable, Miami will switch to a more speed-based running attack with Girard Pringle Jr. with freshman Javian Mallory as the power back. CMU would likely focus more on containing Darian Mensah and the passing game.

What Mario Cristobal said about injuries

Asked about the status of Toney and Fletcher during his press conference Sept. 21, coach Mario Cristobal said "everything looks favorable" regarding their status going forward.

Who benefits if Malachi Toney is out vs Central Michigan?

If Toney is out, Daylyn Upshaw and Cooper Barkate become the primary wide options with more focus funneled toward tight end Elija Lofton . Expect more snaps to Vandrevius Jacobs and freshmen Vance Spafford and Somourian Wingo, as well.

Who benefits if Mark Fletcher is out vs Central Michigan?

If Fletcher sits, Miami will be down their two best running backs. Speedster Girard Pringle Jr. and freshman Javian Mallory would likely split time in the backfield, while Cristobal would likely have no choice but to cycle in beleaguered junior Jordan Lyle .

articles.title: Sixers 3 goals: LeBron James just needs to be himself in Philly
articles.summary: LeBron James just needs to be himself as he gets set to join the Philadelphia 76ers for his 24th season in the league.
articles.body:
In this new series, Sixers Wire looks at the 16 players, per Spotrac, that comprise the Philadelphia 76ers roster — 14 under standard contracts and the two players on two-way deals — and gives each three goals for the 2026-27 season.

The new season begins on Oct. 20, and training camp is right around the corner. Now is the time to begin previewing the new season of adventure that is Sixers basketball.

Up next in this series is megastar LeBron James . The future Hall of Famer joins the Sixers after eight seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers and he continues to be one of the best in the game after averaging 20.9 points, 7.2 assists, and 6.1 rebounds in the 2025-26 season. He will now look to make an impact in Philadelphia .

For James, his three goals are as follows:

For James and the Sixers, the goal is obvious: get to the mountaintop in the NBA. James has been there four times in the past, as he won two titles with the Miami Heat , a title with the Cleveland Cavaliers , and one with the Lakers. While the Sixers were already one of the more talented teams in the league heading into the new season, they don't have those championship habits that James has developed over his career. It will be on James to be the one that sets the tone every single day and shows his teammates the arduous journey of what it takes to win a championship in the NBA. The lessons and examples he can pass down every day will be important for this group to build on.

James has one of the highest IQs a player can have in this game. He has been able to throw teams on his back just by making subtle eye or head movements in an effort to point his teammates in a certain direction to get them open looks within the offensive ecosystem. When considering the offensive talent that will be placed around him in Philadelphia, one has to believe James won't need to be that ruthless scorer as he has had to be in the past. Now, he can settle into more of a playmaking role and make sure Joel Embiid , Jaylen Brown , and Tyrese Maxey get their touches and looks while out on the floor.

Yes, James turns 42 in December. While he has been kicking Father Time's behind in every other aspect, it seems his age is affecting him a bit on the defensive end of the floor as of late. One has to believe that a lesser offensive burden in Philadelphia could make his life a bit easier and allow him to be more focused and active on the defensive end. If the Sixers can get James to even make a few plays in the passing lanes and allow Philadelphia to get out and run, then it will make life that much easier for everybody else within the system. It would allow the Sixers to get into their sets much quicker and allow them to find a rhythm.

articles.title: Karl Mecklenburg previews 'Sunday Night Football,' says it could be Super Bowl preview
articles.summary: Is the Broncos-Rams game a preview of this season's Super Bowl? Karl Mecklenburg believes it could be.
articles.body:
Karl Mecklenburg originally shared this post on his social media pages, and it was re-shared here with permission.

The 2026 Broncos got their first win of the season beating Jacksonville in Denver. They had a short week of preparation after their Monday night loss in Kansas City. The Broncos needed to work on basics anyway. Denver's blocking and tackling was much improved against the Jaguars . They ran the ball successfully with a variety of running backs getting positive carries. Rookie Jonah Coleman looked like a veteran on the last drive, staying in bounds and chewing up the clock. Jaylen Waddle had 138 yards receiving showing Broncos fans why they traded a first-round pick for him. The Broncos offense converted red zone possessions into touchdowns.

Sunday night the Rams are coming to Empower Field. The LA/Denver matchup may be a preview of this season's Super Bowl. It's Broncos Alumni weekend so 45 or so former Broncos (including me) will be at the game. Don't be surprised if you see Nugget and Avalanche players at the game too. The Rams are owned by Kroenke Sports. Like the Nuggets and the Avalanche, Kroenke ownership keeps the Rams in contention every year. Matthew Stafford is a top-notch quarterback, and the Rams have built a strong team around him. articles.title: Tennessee Titans vs. New York Giants: Behind Enemy Lines
articles.summary: Ahead of the Tennessee Titans and New York Giants Week 3 matchup, Titans Wire sat down with Giants Wire to gain insight into the next opponent.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans will face the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, in Week 3. It will mark the Titans' first road game of the season and also give them another opportunity to get one in the win column.

Both the Titans and the Giants are in similar situations in 2026. Well, they were before the Giants lost Jaxson Dart for the season. Both teams have entirely new coaching staffs, and both teams have lots of new faces in the locker room. Both teams were optimistic about 2026 before it started, and now both teams are desperately trying to keep that hope alive.

Ahead of this competitive matchup, Titans Wire sat down with Dan Benton of Giants Wire to gain some insight into the next opponent.

Jameis Winston struggled against the Rams last week. What can we expect to see from him in his first start of 2026?

Benton : I think you'll see Jameis Winston being Jameis Winston with a greater emphasis on not turning the ball over, which is a non-negotiable with John Harbaugh and Matt Nagy. What I wouldn't do -- as so many have -- is overreact to how Winston looked on Monday night. He was thrust into a game unexpectedly early on and had to operate a game plan that had been designed for Jaxson Dart. That came on the heels of a summer in which he took no first-team reps with the other starters, so it wasn't exactly a recipe for success. With a full week under his belt and a game plan designed around his skill set, Winston should look more the part on Sunday afternoon, weather permitting.

Which skill player do you expect to step up this week? What specifically can we expect from this player?

This is going to be a Cam Skattebo game. Nagy already lamented his lack of use in Week 2, and given the early forecast, this game will be decided in the trenches and on the ground. I would expect a heavy dose of Skatt with Ricard leading the way up the middle, and then around the edges. He is sneaky fast and can get going laterally, which is something Najee Harris can't do. Skatt is also sure-handed and a good option out of the backfield, which will play to Winston's strength, with the downfield game likely impacted by rain and wind.

Brian Callahan and Dennard Robinson were both in Tennessee last year. What has their impact been like, and how will their presence affect the game this week?

Callahan seems like he's in an ideal role and made a lot of progress with Dart this offseason. It's a shame we can't see that play out over a full season. Wilson is always a defensive coordinator I've been impressed with, and that hasn't changed over two weeks, despite an ugly outing against Los Angeles . But it's hard to blame him considering he lost his father just days earlier. And while he says there are "no excuses," I think we can all recognize that his mind was likely elsewhere. He works well with the talent he has and builds game plans specific to players' strengths. However, he will be tested this week in the absence of Brian Burns , Paulson Adebo , and other key players banged up.

What's your biggest matchup concern against the Titans?

Jeffery Simmons vs. John Michael Schmitz . Easy. JMS has not developed the way the Giants have hoped, and he hasn't given the team a return on investment. He was dominated by Aaron Donald a week ago, and Simmons has the ability to take over games against inferior players. The Giants will have to scheme around that weakness or risk being dominated at the line of scrimmage in a game that will be decided there.

Given the early weather forecast, this game has a chance to be ugly. Heavy rains and gusty winds will make throwing the ball difficult, and kickoffs and field goals even more difficult. That's actually good news for the Giants, who will be able to ride running back Cam Skattebo until the wheels come off. So long as they can prevent Jeffery Simmons from wrecking the game, Jameis Winston & Co. will come out with a 16-7 win.

articles.title: Little League reflections reveal need to 'keep sports about kids'
articles.summary: USA TODAY's Steve Borelli reflects on how an opportunity to share baseball with his sons became an experience that shaped who he became as a father.
articles.body:
USA TODAY columnist Steve Borelli (aka Coach Steve) spent 10 years coaching his two sons' baseball and basketball teams. He reflects on the years. This story was also publishe d at LittleLeague.org as part of Little League's #LLProudParent content series, which shares first-person reflections on experiences with their child in the Little League program.

Joining Little League was a natural fit for my family. Some of my fondest childhood memories are from being on a baseball diamond with my dad in the dugout. I lived for that experience. So, when I had two sons of my own, getting back to Little League just felt natural.

My coaching experience started with my older son, but I eventually spent time as either a manager or assistant coach for both of my boys in Little League, basketball, and flag football. The decade I spent coaching my sons and watching them move up through the levels of play taught me so much . At the same time, I was building my career as a sportswriter. The shared moments on the diamond with my sons and the lessons I learned from the players and families I worked with each season ultimately led to my weekly sports parenting column, "Ask Coach Steve," with USA TODAY.

What began as an opportunity to share a game I loved with my sons became an experience that shaped not only my career, but who I was as a father. My favorite moments from my sons' Little League years had little to do with the wins and losses I experienced as a coach. Instead, I remember drives home filled with conversations about sportsmanship as they both wrestled with what they could have done differently to prevent a tough loss.

I remember helping them work through disappointment and adversity. My one son was never selected to an All-Star team during his Little League years, but he persevered, and he is now playing at the collegiate level. Teaching them patience and rewarding them for good sportsmanship far outweigh the final score being in your favor at the end of a game.

For parents watching from the stands, my advice is to keep it fun and let them compete. I think back to the times where I would say too much to the hitter who was up to bat instead of letting them figure the situation out for themselves. Those are the moments that we don't realize could be life lessons if we just let them experience it. Letting a kid work through a challenge or a failure can help them better understand the purpose and benefits of the sport they are playing.

We can help guide them through that process from afar. One day, they will look back and realize the lesson they learned in that moment has been carried with them into their adult years. So, let your kids compete. Let them make decisions. Let them work through those difficult moments. Let them fail. Sit back, watch and enjoy the chance to see your kids play.

For the parents who step onto the diamond as a coach, my advice is two-fold. First, as a parent, be open with your kids and allow them to express themselves about what they need from you as both a parent and as a coach. If you just go to the field and yell at them and tell them what they are doing wrong – even if they have success – it will still be a frustrating experience that could lead them to quit.

My second piece of advice is to have an open mind with every kid on the team. It's not just your experience or your kid's experience. It's about every child on that team. Give every player your attention. Give every player opportunity to prove themselves, because even a small moment of success can go a long way to give them the confidence they need to come back next season. Little League is meant to be an inclusive environment where everyone can get something out of it, whether they are the star on the team or someone trying it out for the first time, and it takes the coaches to help create that environment .

After years of coaching, raising two sons, writing about youth sports and talking with families, I always come back to one idea – keep youth sports about the kids . That is a perspective that is lost in today's youth sports climate as parents push their kids to specialize in a sport and apply a ton of pressure to be great.

Last year, I interviewed two-time MLB All-Star Todd Frazier , who competed in the Little League Baseball World Series back in 1998, and he said, "no one's getting scouted at 12-years-old." At the Little League level, our job is to give kids the opportunity to play, learn, experience failure and success and just enjoy being a kid.

Those are the experiences my sons and I were lucky enough to share through Little League, and they are the experience I hope families continue to find on baseball diamonds for generations to come.

Have a story you'd like to share? Feel free to share it, along with any photos that help tell the story, to Media@LittleLeague.org .

Steve Borelli, aka Coach Steve, has been an editor and writer with USA TODAY since 1999. He and his wife, Colleen, are now sports parents to a college and high school baseball player. For his past columns, click here .

articles.title: Lazio Stalwart Reaches Verbal Agreement With Balotelli’s UAE Club
articles.summary: Lazio and Patric could be about to end their 11-year collaboration, with the defender closing in on a move to Al-Ittifaq.The BackgroundThe 33-year-old is a B...
articles.body:
Lazio and Patric could be about to end their 11-year collaboration, with the defender closing in on a move to Al-Ittifaq.

The 33-year-old is a Barcelona youth product who made the move to the Italian capital club in 2015. The centre-back went on to make 244 appearances for the Biancocelesti, but his tally would have been larger if it wasn't for his recurring injury problems.

Patric (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images)

In fact, Gennaro Gattuso wasn't able to rely on the veteran in pre-season, which prompted the decision to drop him from his Serie A squad list alongside Luca Pellegrini . The club left two spots vacant, and one was later filled by Diogo Leite 's late arrival.

Lazio Aiming to Offload Patric in the Coming Days

According to Il Messaggero , Lazio are keen to sell Patric before September 30, when they'll be expected to present their financial statement for the second half of the year. These figures will serve as the basis to determine whether the club will be allowed to operate on the market in January, as the risk of a transfer ban (or another net-zero market) persists.

Patric's age and expiring contract (June 2027) mean he's unlikely to generate a relevant transfer fee. But as the Roman newspaper explains, the defender's sale would allow the Aquile to save €3.5 million in gross salary.

Patric Could Join Mario Balotelli at Al-Ittifaq

While Il Messaggero only mentions that the player has received an offer from a Dubai-based club, Il Corriere dello Sport identifies Patric's suitor as Al-Ittifaq, an ambitious side that plays in UAE's second division. The club is currently coached by former Juventus defender Paolo Montero, and its ranks include former Serie A stars, Mario Balotelli and Douglas Costa .

CdS believes the Spanish defender already has an agreement in principle with Al-Ittifaq, who will try to conclude the operation before the Emirati transfer market closes on Monday. Therefore, the parties will try to finalise the deal in the next 48 hours or so.

Need for another top left-back at Manchester United

Unfortunately, however, a deal for such a player did not go through, after a move for top target Lewis Hall failed to materialise.

While that transfer was to be revisited next year, a move for Hall is no longer on the table. He has since committed his future to Newcastle, publicly highlighting his desire to stay there long term.

As a result, INEOS have had to turn to other targets, and one appealing option is Tyrick Mitchell .

Mitchell is in the final year of his contract at Selhurst Park, and given his quality and Premier League experience, he appeals to the 20-time English champions. They want him, and the player will reportedly find it hard to refuse.

Yet, as hope builds over this transfer, some less pleasing news is emerging from Italy .

Tutto Sport are reporting that, beyond David Raum , who has also been linked with a switch to M16, Juventus also want Mitchell.

They see him as the perfect option to bolster their left-back options. However, while they could also look to sign Mitchell when he becomes a free agent at the end of the season, they know it will be hard to compete with United, or any other top English side, in that race.

As a result, they are keen to move fast and convince Palace to let them sign Mitchell in January.

Whether the Red Devils will move to counter such a move remains to be seen, given the appeal of a free transfer. But if they do not, that could be another top left-back they miss out on.

articles.title: Gyokeres scores for Sweden, still looks miserable
articles.summary: Viktor Gyokeres got the minutes and the goal he needed for Sweden against Romania, but his reaction suggested there is still more to come from the Arsenal fo...
articles.body:
Viktor Gyokeres got the minutes and the goal he needed for Sweden against Romania, but his reaction suggested there is still more to come from the Arsenal forward.

Viktor Gyokeres scored the winner for Sweden against Romania on Friday evening, but the Arsenal forward still looked far from pleased.

With Kai Havertz fit this season, at least until his hamstring went while playing for Germany during the current international break , Gyokeres has found minutes and form hard to come by domestically.

He has played only 29 out of a possible 450 Premier League minutes and has totalled just 207 minutes across all competitions.

Given the stop-start nature of his involvement, it is perhaps unsurprising that he has yet to register a goal or assist for Arsenal this season and has generally looked frustrated when he has been on the pitch.

Unlike for most other Arsenal players, the international break, therefore, was seen as a good thing for Gyokeres.

It is a chance for him to get minutes and find some sharpness.

Even though he found the back of the net in the 43rd minute to win the game 2-1 for his country, he still looked fairly miserable as he did his trademark celebration.

He finished the match as Player of the Match with the highest rating of any player on the pitch, 7.9.

Across 76 minutes, Gyokeres completed 15 of 16 passes, created another chance and scored with the only opportunity that came his way, although the media in Sweden described his performance as 'edgy' at times and criticised his finishing after a second half miss.

articles.title: Liverpool make fresh plans to finally sign long-term target
articles.summary: Over the summer, Liverpool were linked with a whole host of players. Arne Slot was sacked and Andoni Iraola was brought in which meant that plenty of change...
articles.body:
Over the summer, Liverpool were linked with a whole host of players.

Arne Slot was sacked and Andoni Iraola was brought in which meant that plenty of change was already scheduled to take place.

And, while things have started off quite slowly with only a few wins, the fact that the Reds are still unbeaten across all competitions is fairly impressive.

Indeed, Liverpool did manage to bring in a fair few new faces over the summer but, it still feels like more additions and potentially even exits are needed.

So, the fact that new links with players are continuing to emerge despite the transfer window being shut is rather reassuring with a previously-linked player now making his way back onto the Reds' shortlist.

Liverpool want to sign Micky van de Ven from Tottenham again

One of the main areas of Liverpool's team that needed upgrading in the summer was their defence.

Ibrahima Konate and Andy Robertson both exited Anfield and, while the Scotsman was replaced by Kostas Tsimikas , the Reds still needed a new centre-back which is where Jeremy Jacquet came in .

However, even after both of these moves, thanks to injuries and unavailability, Liverpool were still short at the back which resulted in Ronald Araujo joining on a season-long loan.

And, to the surprise of many, the Uruguayan has been pivotal to the Reds this term.

But, before Araujo and Jacquet were signed, many other players emerged as potential options with Micky van de Ven being one of them .

Unfortunately, that deal never came to fruition and the Dutchman ended up signing a contract extension with Tottenham but, since Spurs have failed to meet expectations once again, it seems like Liverpool are about to try and make a move for the Dutchman once again.

"Liverpool are plotting a move to sign Tottenham Hotspur star Micky van de Ven as they put plans in place to strengthen at the back," Football Insider wrote .

" Andoni Iraola 's side are making long-term plans to sign a new centre-back as they prepare for Virgil van Dijk to leave the club upon the expiry of his contract next summer.

"The centre-back's fellow countryman has been high on their list for a long time, and following Tottenham's slow start to the new season, they could try to take advantage.

"Roberto De Zerbi's side are understood to be reluctant to lose their captain, and will demand a significant fee, especially if they are to sell to a Premier League rival.

"Van de Ven, however, is believed to be open to a move to Anfield given Tottenham's recent struggles and would welcome the opportunity to discuss terms over a move."

Liverpool signing Micky van de Ven would be a bold move

On paper, Van de Ven looks like he'd be a perfect signing for Liverpool.

However, since he's only just signed a new deal with Spurs and hasn't really been in the best run of form lately, it doesn't feel as good as what it did last season.

Since the Dutchman has extended his contract, it's very likely that he'd cost a hefty chunk of change for Liverpool to bring in.

But, with his lightning-quick speed, his versatility and experience, it is probably going to be hard to find another player who ticks all of those boxes.

That is, especially since left-back is a major problem area for Liverpool at the moment.

Obviously, many changes are expected to take place at Anfield over the next few months so the rumour mill is very likely to go into overdrive.

However, as long as Iraola and Julian Ward both know who they want to sign and for how much, that's all that fans can really ask for.

articles.title: Dexter Lawrence is adding, among many things, personality to the Bengals defense
articles.summary: This Bengals’ defensive line is having fun feasting and trash talking.
articles.body:
Zac Taylor is in a unique position. He's the head coach of the Bengals and their offensive play-caller.

In his position, Taylor, like a CEO, is also in charge of managing this team's personalities. Most of those personalities have been on offense in Taylor's tenure.

Now, the defense has some. Not only is the Bengals' defense revived. It has personality , especially up front and with Dexter Lawrence .

Lawrence is the tone-setter of the Bengals' defense. That comes in the form of on-field production, but it also comes with having a little fun on the field trash-talking.

"He just loves it. I think he's contributed to the personality of our defense," Taylor said after Friday's practice. "Not only are they talented and confident, and playing with this really good chemistry, but they've got a really big personality as a whole, and he's obviously a big part of this, and that's what's fun."

Lawrence was mic'd up during the Bengals' 20-6 win over the Houston Texans in Week 2. It was incredible to listen to, with Lawrence demonstrating elite trash-talking abilities.

It's something we haven't really seen from a Bengals' defense in quite some time. The S.W.A.T. Team had personality back in the 80s, but Bengals' defenses since really haven't it… until now.

"With the mic'd up stuff, everybody gets to see kind of what we see from him, (defensive tackle) Jonathan Allen , and everybody kind of combining together," Taylor said. "And it probably gets a couple of the other guys out of their shell a little bit."

Don't be surprised if you see other mic'd-up segments and soundbites from the Bengals or NFL Films showcasing Lawrence and the Bengals' defensive line trash-talking their opponents. The Bengals' defensive line is getting a lot of attention. They have talented players, but they also have players with personalities.

articles.body:
Bodybuilding fans, rejoice — it's finally that time of year. Mr. Olympia returns to Las Vegas for its 62nd annual competition this week.

When it comes to professional bodybuilding, there's truly no bigger stage than this. The best and most accomplished athletes in the sport will soon head to Sin City to compete for the iconic titles of Mr. and Ms. Olympia, with events taking place over the course of three days.

In last year's competition, Derek Lunsford returned to glory, reclaiming bragging rights and the $600,000 prize for the second time in his career.. Lunsford will be back this week, going up against 2024 champion Samson Dauda, Nick Walker and more. 2022 champion Hadi Choopan will be noticeably absent, as he is experiencing issues with his UAE visa.

As for the women, Andrea Shaw remains a dominant force. The six-time champion has won the Ms. Olympia title every year since 2020, and it doesn't look like she'll be slowing down any time soon.

Here is everything you need to know about Mr. Olympia 2026, including a full schedule and list of participants for the annual bodybuilding competition.

Dates: Friday, Sept, 25 - Saturday, Sept. 26

This year, Mr. Olympia will be held at Palms Casino Resort Las Vegas. The finals for Ms. Olympia and Mr. Olympia will take place on Friday and Saturday, respectively.

Ms. Olympia finals/Mr. Olympia pre-judging

Mr. Olympia will not be available to watch on a national TV channel. Viewers can live stream the event on OlympiaTV , which will be completely free for fans this year.

Who is competing in Mr. and Ms. Olympia?

In order to qualify for events, competitors must meet the requirements set by the IFBB Professional League. 22 men qualified for Mr. Olympia, while ten women qualified for Ms. Olympia.

Lunsford is the defending Mr. Olympia champion and will be looking for his third title this year. Dauda won in 2024, but placed fourth last year, so he will surely be hungry to redeem himself. Chinedu Obiekea — or "Andrew Jacked" is also someone to look out for.

Shaw is competing for a seventh straight Ms. Olympia title.

What are the other events held during Mr. Olympia weekend?

There are a few other events beyond the typical Mr. and Ms. Olympia contests.

The other events for men are 212 Olympia, Men's Physique Olympia, Classic Physique Olympia and Wheelchair Olympia.

The other events for women are Figure Olympia, Fitness Olympia, Bikini Olympia, Women's Physique Olympia, Wellness Olympia and Wheelchair Olympia.

The total purse has not yet been announced, but the final figure could land between $1.5 million and $2 million.

The money will be split between the top finishers. In 2025, Lunsford took home $600,000, while the second- and third-place finishers earned $200,000 and $100,000, respectively.

articles.body:
Hassan Celtic riddle as he starts for Egypt despite fake injury claim, whilst Yang also revealed to be struggling with hamstring issue…

13th September 2026; Ibrox; Scottish League Cup Football, Rangers versus Celtic; Haissem Hassan of Celtic. Photo Vagelis Georgariou

Despite reports coming from The Scottish Sun yesterday of Haissem Hassan being ruled out of the Egyptian national squad through an 'intense injury' the 24 year old remarkably played 60 minutes for the his nation in Friday's AFCON qualifier against Angola.

The story posted on The Scottish Sun has now been removed.

Haissem Hassan of Celtic is challenged by Daniel Arzani of Ferencvaros during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Celtic FC and Ferencvarosi TC at Celtic Park on September 17, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Egypt manager Hossam Hassan had earlier being reported to indicated that the Celtic winger was unavailable for selection. The manager was quoted as saying: "Haissem Hassan is receiving intensive treatment just now. But I am not worried about his absence because we have a lot of excellent players to replace him.

"Haissem is a vital technical asset for our long-term vision, but his recent injury made it impossible for him to join us for this camp."

Haissem Hassan of Egypt competes for the ball against Julian Alvarez and Nicolas Tagliafico of Argentina during the FIFA World Cup 2026 Round of 16 match between Argentina and Egypt at Atlanta Stadium on July 07, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Buda Mendes/Getty Images)

However the Egyptian manager's quotes apparently were lost in translation or became the victim of tabloid skullduggery in the search for clicks.

A more accurate translation looks more like this: "Today, for example, Haissem Hassan is coming. You surely followed him in the last match at Celtic, he was injured.

"So we're trying to have quick treatment and he might not start. Maybe. Until today, he is still doing sessions with the medical staff, intensively, in the hope that, god willing, he will be available. If he isn't, I won't worry. This is the Egypt national team."

Haissem Hassan of Egypt controls the ball during the FIFA World Cup 2026 Round of 32 match between Australia and Egypt at Dallas Stadium on July 03, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

So despite these inaccurate and misleading claims the 24-year-old started the game which finished 0-0 in attack alongside former Liverpool star Mo Salah . Both players were substituted after playing around an hour in the match that ended 0-0.

Egypt are due face South Sudan and Celtic will be keeping a keen eye on the fitness of Hassan. His fitness will be closely monitored, especially given Celtic's current situation with wingers.

However, another Celtic winger, Yang, recently revealed he is struggling with a hamstring problem after missing South Korea 's Asian Games quarter-final win over Vietnam .

5th September 2026; The Marbill Coaches Stadium, Paisley, Scottish Premiership, St Mirren versus Celtic; Yang Hyun jun of Celtic celebrates after he shoots and scores in the 68th minute to make it 2-1 to Celtic. Photo Vagelis Georgariou

He said after the match: "I have a minor injury to my hamstring. Right now, I am preparing with the goal of reaching the semi-finals and the finals.

"I was selected as a wild card, but since I haven't been in good physical condition recently and now I'm on top of that with an injury, I feel really sorry for my teammates. I also feel like I'm not being of any help."

5th September 2026; The Marbill Coaches Stadium, Paisley, Scotland ; Scottish Premiership Football, St Mirren versus Celtic; Yang Hyun jun of Celtic celebrates after he shoots and scores in the 68th minute to make it 2-1 to Celtic

It's good to see that Hassan isn't injured despite being led to believe otherwise. But the Yang situation is a bit of a worry, especially since how valuable he's been to the side since the start of the campaign.

articles.body: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua finally appeared to have their long-awaited heavyweight showdown secured after the fight was officially announced for December 11. The all-British clash is scheduled to take place at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium after months of difficult negotiations over the venue and other details.However, the excitement has been replaced by fresh uncertainty. Fury has now claimed that Joshua and his promoter Eddie Hearn are trying to pull out of the fight. The former heavyweight champion made the allegations in a video message, just days after the official announcement.Tyson Fury claims Anthony Joshua and Eddie Hearn are trying to pull out of the fightTyson Fury has sensationally claimed that his fight with Anthony Joshua could be called off despite the December 11 date being officially announced.“Breaking news, Anthony Joshua and Eddie Hearn are trying to pull out the fight. They’re saying they’re not going to fight now. It’s mainly to do with Eddie Hearn’s ego. He’s making up a million different things and threatening ‘we’re not gonna fight’,” said Fury.Fury then turned his attention directly towards Joshua.He added, “Now the Gypsy King is coming back to the United Kingdon to thrash you in front of all my fans in Wales, and now you are making a million excuses. Now you’ve got Turki Alalshikh finding alternative, real men who will fight at the drop of a hat. I hope you are happy.”Sky Sports reported that Matchroom Sport had been contacted for comment following Fury’s claims.The comments come only two days after the heavyweight blockbuster was officially confirmed. Turki Alalshikh announced that Fury and Joshua will meet at Principality Stadium in Cardiff on December 11. The fight will also be streamed globally on Netflix.The bout has been in discussion for years. Fury and Joshua are both former heavyweight world champions, but they have never faced each other professionally.Negotiations became particularly complicated over the location. Several venues were discussed before Cardiff was selected. The Principality Stadium has also hosted Joshua twice, including his fights against Carlos Takam and Joseph Parker.There have also been concerns surrounding both fighters’ recent bouts.Joshua’s July comeback fight against Kristian Prenga almost ended in a major upset. Prenga knocked Joshua down twice in the opening round, but Joshua recovered and stopped him in the second round.Fury’s return has followed a different path. He came back after a year away from boxing and defeated Arslanbek Makhmudov by unanimous decision in April. He then fought Mariusz Wach in Thailand in July and stopped the veteran in the seventh round.The latest controversy therefore comes at a crucial stage of the promotion. Fury and Joshua are scheduled to appear together at a press conference in London on September 30.For now, the official event remains scheduled for December 11 in Cardiff. articles.title: Clemson's revival continues at Cal. Is Dabo Swinney's team back?
articles.summary: Clemson's win streak reached three games with a victory at Cal, but flaws remain as Dabo Swinney's team searches for answers.
articles.body:
The last time Clemson played in the Bay Area, Trevor Lawrence led the Tigers to a national championship on Jan. 7, 2019 to cap off a perfect season.

In 2026, Clemson returned when things are drastically different — but it again left the Golden State a late-night winner.

Dabo Swinney and Co. made the 2,200-mile trip out west for a game that kicked off at 10:30 p.m. ET back at home, and while it again wasn't pretty, the Tigers held on in another defensive slugfest with a 24-10 victory over Cal on Friday, Sept. 25.

Week 4 bold predictions: Ole Miss, LSU on upset alert

After the embarrassing season-opening loss to LSU , Clemson (3-1) has won three straight games, and more importantly, are off to a 2-0 start to its ACC schedule. That's now 16 straight seasons with at least a three-game win streak for the Tigers.

"We're just finding a way to keep winning some games," Swinney said on the ESPN broadcast.

While it's the bounce back you'd want following a rough start, there is plenty of reason to question if Clemson is actually turning things around to be a legit contender. Those reasons were fully on display all the way through 2 a.m. ET at California Memorial Stadium.

Another win in the Golden State was all thanks to the Clemson defense.

It was facing a prolific offense, with Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele leading a Golden Bears passing attack that was averaging 327 yards in the air this season, 14th-best in FBS. Against the Tigers, there was no sight of that.

Sagapolutele was rudely introduced to Tom Allen's defense with an interception on his second throw of the game. From that moment, it was a struggle as the left-handed gunslinger was kept in check all night. He was pressured immensely, but even when he did get time, he wasn't making great decisions or getting the ball where it needed to.

It forced Cal to try and generate offense on the ground, and it had some moments with Adam Mohammed . However, he hurt his leg on a tackle and the rest of the rushing group couldn't pick it up in his absence.

And to cap it off, Sagapolutele's last throw of the game was picked off to seal the win. He finished the night 16-for-29 for a career-low 119 yards and two interceptions.

Cal's lone touchdown came off a fumble recovery, meaning the Clemson defense has gone seven straight quarters without giving up a touchdown. The unit is starting to flex its muscle and make quarterbacks have nightmares.

The bad: Tait Reynolds and the Clemson offense

Make no mistake, the offense in this game wasn't pretty. The Clemson defense has gotten better, but the offense has yet to figure it out.

It all starts with freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds, who clearly still has a long way to go to live up to the high potential he came into Clemson with. He had a real rough start by throwing an interception on the opening drive on a bad decision from a trick play, and later in the first quarter, he coughed up the ball and Cal linebacker Kamar Mothudi ran it back 33 yards for the touchdown.

He finished with just 108 passing yards, the fewest of the three games he's played the majority of for Clemson. That's not going to help a passing offense that entered the night 112th in the country with 172.3 yards per game.

The Tigers did get three touchdowns, but one of them was thanks to a blazing punt return for a score from Bryant Wesco Jr. The first touchdown of the night was thanks to several Cal penalties keeping the Tigers offense on the field, and with just under three minutes left, Clemson running back Gideon Davidson broke free for a 75-yard touchdown run for the dagger.

Plus, the red zone opportunities need to be converted. Clemson has been inside the opponent's 20-yard line 11 times this season, and while its scored on 10 of those chances, only four have been touchdowns.

Whether you believe the Swinney's team has actually bounced back or not, we're all surely about to find out.

One could very well argue Clemson has benefited from a softer schedule, playing Georgia Southern, North Carolina and Cal, all teams not on the same talent level or still in the middle of building up their programs. Even then, none of the wins were impressive and had you thinking the dominant Tigers of years past were back.

Next up for Clemson is No. 5 Miami, where that defense will get another reality check against Darian Mensah , Malachi Toney and all of the star-studded Hurricanes.

In what is easily the biggest home game of the season, Clemson will have to put up a much better fight than it did against LSU to rid itself of the fraud allegations. Another crushing defeat and the calls for Swinney to move on will only get louder. Win, or even play it close, and the old dog shows maybe it does have some fight left in him.

Because unlike the late-night trip Friday, Clemson fans and a whole lot more people are going to be wide awake waiting to find out.

"We're just happy to get the win, and hopefully somebody stayed up back home to watch it," Swinney said.
